_note: v3.7: longer visual descriptions in the best zero-shot setup (taxonomy and symptoms as separate, equally weighted prompts). Single change from v3.6 (HM 11.9% top-1 / 38.1% top-5): the visual descriptions are replaced by longer ones (knowledge/disease_descriptions_long_v1.json, mean 20.9 words vs 8.4; written from general knowledge, unverified). Zero-shot has no validation split, so the comparison is on the same test images; about a point either way is within what wording alone can shift.
_result: Longer visual descriptions also hurt the best setup: harmonic mean 10.1% top-1 / 37.8% top-5 vs v3.6's 11.9% / 38.1%. Same pattern as v3.8: the best SEEN zero-shot accuracy so far (12.0%, seen disease 18.4%) but unseen top-1 drops (8.7% vs 14.1%; grape_black_rot 39% -> 14%). Conclusion from v3.7/v3.8: short, distinctive symptom descriptions transfer better to unseen pairs than long detailed ones; extra detail helps recognise seen pairs but makes descriptions of different diseases more alike. v3.6 (short symptoms + taxonomy as separate prompts) stays the best zero-shot configuration.
